packageRules.description: Keep the echo/v5 engine and its OpenTelemetry companion on one PR so the engine and its instrumentation always update together.

Type the go-bricks-migrate CLI's self-pin as 'chore' so it does not cut a framework release. tools/migration is the only module that depends on go-bricks, and config:recommended's :semanticPrefixFixDepsChoreOthers types dependency updates as 'fix' — which release-please counts as version-bumping for the root module. That made catching the pin up self-defeating: pinning the CLI to v0.58.1 (#960) released framework v0.58.2 (#962, whose entire changelog was that one line), which re-staled the pin and the tools/migration/v* tag the drift check watches (#958). 'chore' does not bump because release-please's default versioning strategy advances the version only on feat/fix/breaking; that is what breaks the loop. release-please-config.json separately marks chore hidden, which affects only changelog rendering — un-hiding it would not re-arm this. Scoped to this one package on purpose: every other fix(deps) carries real content and must keep bumping, since release-cli.sh requires the CLI tag to equal the pinned framework version, so framework releases are what mint the CLI's next releasable number.

Hold the Oracle driver on go-ora v2 until upstream ships the FastLogin cookie-replay fix. v3.0.1 breaks every connection after the first in a process: v3 added a process-global cookieStore whose replayed handshake truncates OracleVersion (7230/8030/8100) through uint8, so the server closes the socket mid-handshake; because that never yields driver.ErrBadConn the driver's own retry never fires and the poisoned cookie is never evicted. database/sql hits this as soon as a pool opens its second physical connection. Measured against gvenzl/oracle-free:23.26.2-slim on 2026-07-25: v2.9.0 integration suite green, an imports-only v3.0.1 rewrite fails every connection-opening test with a bare EOF, and FAST LOGIN=false restores them. Upstream sijms/go-ora#732 is fixed on master (a968e590) but NOT released — the newest tag is still v3.0.1. Delete this rule once a tagged release carries the fix, then redo the import rewrite (go-bricks#756).

Label Flyway CLI bumps and attach the re-pin steps. The hosted Renovate app moves only FLYWAY_VERSION; Redgate publishes no .sha256 to pin against, so the ci-v2.yml SHA256 gate keeps the PR red until a maintainer verifies the tarball's signature and re-pins the checksum by hand. The label makes those PRs filterable; the note saves rediscovering the procedure. The fingerprint is the key that also signed flyway-core on Maven Central (6.0.0 through 11.8.2); if Redgate rotates it, check the new one against an independent source like that before trusting it.
prBodyNotes:
**Flyway re-pin needed.** CI stays red until `FLYWAY_SHA256` matches the new tarball; that red is the intended alert.

1. Download `https://download.red-gate.com/maven/release/com/redgate/flyway/flyway-commandline/{{{newVersion}}}/flyway-commandline-{{{newVersion}}}-linux-x64.tar.gz` and the `.asc` next to it. Do not use the GitHub release asset: it is a different artifact.
2. Import Redgate's Flyway key by fingerprint (`gpg --keyserver keys.openpgp.org --recv-keys F79157DB93697AA32CD4C46CC485C5A843FADB15`; it expires 2027-04-24), then run `gpg --status-fd 1 --verify flyway-commandline-{{{newVersion}}}-linux-x64.tar.gz.asc flyway-commandline-{{{newVersion}}}-linux-x64.tar.gz` (always name both files) and require a `VALIDSIG` line carrying that fingerprint.
3. Set `FLYWAY_SHA256` next to `FLYWAY_VERSION` in `.github/workflows/ci-v2.yml` to the verified tarball's `sha256sum`.
4. Copy the same version and checksum into the Install Flyway example in `wiki/multi_tenant_migration.md`.
5. Touch the `migration/testdata/flyway` fixtures only if `framework-integration-test` then fails parsing the new CLI's JSON output; re-capture them from it.

customManagers.description: Bump the go-run-pinned security scanners (GOVULNCHECK_VERSION / GOSEC_VERSION) in both Makefiles. These are 'go run <module>@<version>' literals that Renovate's gomod manager cannot see, so they drift silently (govulncheck rotted from v1.1.4 well behind latest before this manager existed). The inline '# renovate:' annotation above each pin supplies the datasource + depName.

Bump the go-run-pinned apidiff tool in the API-compatibility CI gate (.github/workflows). The 'go install <module>@<version>' literal in a workflow run: string is invisible to Renovate's gomod manager, so it drifts silently. The inline '# renovate:' annotation above the pin supplies the datasource + depName.
matchStrings: # renovate: datasource=(?<datasource>\S+) depName=(?<depName>\S+)( versioning=(?<versioning>\S+))?\s+run: go install \S+@(?<currentValue>\S+)

customManagers.description: Bump testcontainers image tags pinned as Go string literals in testing/containers. These defaults are invisible to every built-in manager, so they rot silently (RabbitMQ sat on EOL 3.13.7 until 2026-08). The inline '// renovate:' annotation above each pin supplies the datasource + depName; the field shape is generic (any string field, like the Makefile manager's \w+_VERSION) so a field rename cannot silently detach the pin; docker versioning keeps the '-management-alpine'-style suffix stable across bumps. Only annotated pins are managed — annotate the other containers to opt them in.

Bump annotated 'docker pull' pins in workflow run: scripts — the CI cache pre-warm duplicates the testing/containers image tags, and shell literals are invisible to built-in managers (the RabbitMQ copy sat stale next to the bumped Go pin until both were annotated). Same-depName updates land in one Renovate PR, keeping the pre-pull and the Go default in lockstep.

Track the CI-pinned Flyway CLI version. Flyway 12.x tarballs ship only from Redgate's server (Maven Central stopped at 11.8.2), but flyway/flyway still tags GitHub releases (flyway-X.Y.Z), so github-releases tracks the version number; the SHA256 gate makes the resulting bump PR fail CI until a maintainer re-pins the checksum (the needs-flyway-sha packageRule lists the steps) — that failing PR is the intended alert. The version capture accepts only plain X.Y.Z tags, so a malformed upstream tag never reaches the workflow or the PR note.
